item.title: Chaos and bifurcations in continuous language-model feedback
item.description: arXiv:2610.31692v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Feeding a pretrained language model the expected embedding of its own next-token distribution turns it into a discrete-time dynamical system with continuous states. Across Qwen2.5, OLMo-2 and Llama-3 models from 0.5B to 72B parameters, temperature and activation steering move this loop between repeating text and chaos, with positive finite-time Lyapunov exponents. The loop's derivative factorizes into the inverse temperature, the covariance of token embeddings under the next-token distribution (a cross-covariance for untied embeddings) and the network's Jacobian. In one model studied in detail, along recorded orbits, the growth that steering adds comes mainly from the readout, where next tokens compete. The periodic windows show the quantitative signatures of low-dimensional maps, from saddle-node scaling and Feigenbaum's constant to shrimp-shaped domains; passage times predicted in advance from the model's derivatives came within one return-map iterate of the measured passage times in 42 of 48 cases over two prospective stages (24 and 18 of 24), and interval arithmetic proves attracting periodic orbits of the full transformer map. Numerical reproducibility depends on the dynamical regime: changing only the batch layout changed the text of 173 of 192 chaotic float64 loops in the smallest model, compared with only 7 of 192 periodic ones. These results show that bifurcation theory can make quantitative predictions about continuous language-model feedback, with rigorous guarantees for selected periodic orbits of the full transformer.
item.dc:creator: Timothy D. Jones

item.title: Spatiotemporal Dynamics of Conway's Game of Life in the Entropy--Complexity Plane
item.description: arXiv:2610.31708v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the dynamics of Conway's Game of Life (GoL) through the lens of Ordinal Pattern analysis. Each GoL generation is transformed into a one-dimensional time series, from which ordinal patterns are extracted to characterize its underlying dynamics. The resulting ordinal distributions are then represented in the Entropy--Statistical Complexity ($H \times C$) plane, enabling a quantitative analysis of the system's evolution. We evaluate different encoding strategies, including patch sizes and linearization methods, and assess their impact on the resulting $H \times C$ trajectories. Finally, we characterize the emergent dynamics in terms of convergence behavior, trajectory patterns, and statistical complexity, showing how the proposed entropy--complexity framework provides insights into the dynamics of cellular automata.
item.dc:creator: Lucas Malacarne Astore, Alejandro C. Frery, Petr\^onio C\^andido de Lima e Silva, Frederico Gadelha Guimar\~aes

item.title: Reservoir as a Dynamical System: A Tutorial Review
item.description: arXiv:2610.32421v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This brief tutorial review examines the operation of reservoir computing from the standpoint of nonlinear dynamics and provides a concise overview of recent advances in the field. We begin by delineating the predictive capabilities of reservoir systems, followed by a succinct yet sufficient introduction to the nonlinear dynamical systems techniques that will be employed throughout this article to elucidate reservoir functioning. Subsequently, we describe reservoir operation using these techniques in the context of successful prediction, accompanied by all necessary implementation codes. The objective of this article is to offer a practical guide to the implementation of reservoir computing while, from a nonlinear dynamics perspective, explaining the mechanisms by which reservoirs achieve accurate predictions.
item.dc:creator: Sarika Jalan, Ling Feng, Dishant Sisodia, Kohei Nakajima

item.title: Chaos Made Visible: Active particles trace Lorenz-like attractors in physical space
item.description: arXiv:2610.32640v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chaotic attractors are typically visualized in an abstract phase space. Here we show that an orientable active particle moving through a steady, two-dimensional, multivortex flow can trace a Lorenz-like chaotic attractor in its real space trajectory. Despite the flow being strictly time independent, coupling between particle position and orientation creates a three-dimensional nonlinear dynamical system. For suitable particle shape and swimming speed, the trajectory organizes into a striking two-lobed geometry reminiscent of the classical Lorenz attractor. A structured first return map, positive largest Lyapunov exponent, and a broadband power spectrum establish that the underlying motion is chaotic. Varying the swimming speed reveals a rich sequence of dynamical regimes as self-propulsion breaks streamline confinement and reorganizes the particle motion. Our results demonstrate how an internal orientational degree of freedom can make chaotic dynamics directly visible in physical space, allowing a single active particle to trace a chaotic attractor as it moves through an otherwise steady flow.
item.dc:creator: Rahil N. Valani, Ekashman Tiwari, Aritra Roy

item.title: Universal Boolean Computation in Negatively Coupled Circle Map Lattices
item.description: arXiv:2610.16290v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the computational capabilities of a one-dimensional lattice of negatively coupled circle maps in its traveling wave regime. We interpret propagating waves as information carriers and exploit their interactions to implement Boolean logic. The logical states are encoded by the propagation direction of the traveling waves, while the presence or absence of a wave at a designated output location represents the logical output. Using controlled wave collisions, we demonstrate the realization of NAND and NOR gates along with other basic gates. Since NAND and NOR operations are functionally complete, the results establish that the traveling wave regime of the negatively coupled circle-map lattice supports universal Boolean computation in principle. The demonstrated logical operations remain valid over a finite range of the coupling strength \epsilon and map parameter \omega, indicating robustness of the computational scheme to parameter variations. Our results therefore demonstrate that computational functionality can emerge from the collective nonlinear dynamics of a coupled map lattice, providing a con- nection between the dynamical properties of traveling wave states and collision based information processing.
item.dc:creator: Priyanka D. Bhoyar, Prashant M. Gade
